steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the fs (file system) module using require()
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import the built-in fs module. This will give you access to file system operations.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing a built-in module
const path = require('path');
steps.expectedOutcome: The fs module will be imported and available for use in your error handling code.
successCriteria: The fs module is imported using require('fs')
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the fs module. This gives you access to Node.js file system operations which we'll use for error handling examples.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using require('fs') to import the file system module.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to use require('fs') to import the built-in file system module.

steps.title: Create a synchronous function that reads a file
steps.instruction: Define a function named readFileSync that takes a filename parameter and uses fs.readFileSync to read the file synchronously. Return the file content.
steps.hint: Use the fs module you imported earlier. The function should take one parameter and return the result of fs.readFileSync.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named readFileSync is defined that can read files synchronously using the fs module.
successCriteria: The readFileSync function is defined with a filename parameter, uses fs.readFileSync, and returns the file content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the synchronous file reading function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function uses fs.readFileSync and returns the result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Check that it's named readFileSync, takes a filename parameter, and uses fs.readFileSync to read the file.

steps.title: Add try-catch block to handle synchronous errors
steps.instruction: Inside your synchronous file reading function, wrap the fs.readFileSync call in a try block and add a catch block to handle potential errors.
steps.hint: Use try { ... } catch (error) { ... } syntax. Inside the catch block, you can log the error or handle it appropriately.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will have a try block containing the file reading operation and a catch block to handle errors.
successCriteria: The function contains a try block with fs.readFileSync inside it and a catch block that handles errors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added error handling with try-catch to your synchronous file reading function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both a try block (with fs.readFileSync inside) and a catch block to handle errors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't have proper try-catch error handling. Remember to wrap the file reading operation in a try block and add a catch block to handle errors.

steps.title: Log success and error messages in the try-catch
steps.instruction: Inside the try block of your readFileSyncExample function, add a console.log statement that logs a success message when the file is read successfully. Inside the catch block, add a console.log statement that logs the error message.
steps.hint: Use console.log() with a descriptive string in the try block. In the catch block, you can log the error parameter (e.g., console.log(error)).
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will log a success message when the file read operation succeeds and an error message when it fails, making the error handling visible.
successCriteria: The try block contains a console.log statement with a success message. The catch block contains a console.log statement that logs the error parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added proper logging for both success and error cases, which is essential for debugging and monitoring.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both a success log in the try block and an error log in the catch block.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added console.log statements in both the try and catch blocks with appropriate messages.

steps.title: Create an asynchronous function that reads a file
steps.instruction: Define an async function named readFileAsync that takes a filename parameter. Place it after the existing synchronous function.
steps.hint: Use the async keyword before function to make it asynchronous. The function should accept one parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an async function named readFileAsync that accepts a filename parameter, ready for implementing file reading logic.
successCriteria: The code contains an async function named readFileAsync with one parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created an async function for file operations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function is async and has the correct name and parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check that it's async, named readFileAsync, and accepts a filename parameter.

steps.title: Use try-catch with await for async error handling
steps.instruction: Inside the readFileAsync function, add a try-catch block and use await with fs.promises.readFile() to handle asynchronous errors.
steps.hint: Remember to use the async keyword on the function and await inside the try block. Use fs.promises.readFile() for the asynchronous file reading.
steps.expectedOutcome: The readFileAsync function should have a try-catch block that uses await with fs.promises.readFile() to handle asynchronous file reading errors.
successCriteria: The readFileAsync function contains a try-catch block with await fs.promises.readFile() inside the try block.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented async error handling with try-catch and await.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both the try and catch blocks, and use await with fs.promises.readFile().
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a try-catch block inside readFileAsync and used await with fs.promises.readFile().

steps.title: Log results from the async function
steps.instruction: Inside the readFileAsync function, add console.log statements in both the try and catch blocks to log success and error messages.
steps.hint: Use console.log with descriptive messages in both blocks. In the try block, log a success message when the file is read. In the catch block, log the error message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The readFileAsync function will have console.log statements in both try and catch blocks to handle success and error outcomes.
successCriteria: The readFileAsync function contains console.log statements in both the try and catch blocks.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added proper logging to handle both success and error outcomes in your async function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have console.log statements in both the try and catch blocks of the readFileAsync function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The readFileAsync function should have console.log statements in both the try and catch blocks to log success and error messages.

steps.title: Create a function that throws a custom error
steps.instruction: Define a function called validateInput that throws a new Error with a custom message if the input is invalid. The function should accept one parameter and throw an error when the parameter is falsy.
steps.hint: Create a function that checks if the input exists (is truthy). If it's falsy, throw a new Error with a message like 'Invalid input'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a validateInput function that throws a custom error when given invalid input.
successCriteria: The validateInput function is defined, accepts one parameter, and throws a new Error with a custom message when the input is falsy.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a function that throws a custom error. This is a fundamental pattern for validating inputs in Node.js.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function throws a new Error with a custom message when the input is invalid (falsy).
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a function called validateInput that checks if the input is falsy and throws a new Error with a custom message.

steps.title: Call the custom error function with error handling
steps.instruction: Inside the validateInput function, add a try-catch block that calls validateInput with an invalid input and logs any caught errors.
steps.hint: Wrap the function call in a try block and use console.error to log the error in the catch block.
steps.expectedOutcome: The validateInput function will now include error handling logic that demonstrates catching and logging custom errors.
successCriteria: validateInput contains a try-catch block that calls itself with invalid input and logs the caught error.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added error handling to the custom error function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both try and catch blocks with proper error logging.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validateInput function should contain a try-catch block that calls itself and logs errors.

steps.title: Create the main function to demonstrate all error handling
steps.instruction: Create a function named main that calls readFileSyncExample, readFileAsync, and validateInput with proper error handling for each.
steps.hint: Define a function called main that uses try-catch blocks to call each of the three functions you've created, logging results appropriately.
steps.expectedOutcome: A main function that demonstrates error handling by calling all three functions with proper try-catch blocks.
successCriteria: The main function is defined and calls readFileSyncExample, readFileAsync, and validateInput with error handling for each.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main function that demonstrates all error handling concepts together.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your main function calls all three functions with proper error handling.
steps.feedbackWrong: The main function should be defined and call readFileSyncExample, readFileAsync, and validateInput with error handling.
